resources.string: Tap a question to see the answer
How do I add a meal?
On the home screen tap the add-food button, find a product via search or barcode scanner, set the portion weight and save. The entry appears in the day\'s diary.
Where does my calorie goal come from?
It\'s calculated from your profile (sex, age, height, weight, activity and goal) using the Mifflin–St Jeor formula. Update your profile and the goal recalculates.
On the water card use the quick-add buttons (e.g. +200 ml) or set a custom amount. Hold a glass to remove an entry. The water goal is based on your profile.
How do I add or change weight?
In Analytics enter a new weight and tap Done on the keyboard or the save button. The chart shows the trend. You can set a target weight and see an estimate.
What are levels and how do I earn XP?
XP is earned for unlocked achievements and for days you met your calorie and water goals. Levels unlock rewards — animated avatar frames and companions.
How do I build a weekly menu?
In the meal plan section pick a diet type and tap «Build weekly menu». You can reshuffle with «Build another menu» and load any day into your plan.
How do I make a PDF report?
Settings → «Data» → «Export to PDF». Choose a period (week or month). The report includes charts, weight, spending, frequent foods and a nutrition summary.
How do I change language or currency?
Settings → «Language» and «Currency». Currency defaults to your language but can be set manually.
All data is stored locally on your device in an encrypted database. It is not sent to any server. You can back it up via export in the «Data» section.
In the measurements section tap a body part on the figure or pick it from the list, then enter the value in centimeters. History and progress are in measurement analytics.

Gaining muscle needs a calorie surplus and enough protein (≈1.6–2 g per kg of body weight). Eat regularly and add snacks. Strength training + nutrition = muscle growth.
To stay in shape, keep your macros balanced and calories steady. Combine protein, complex carbs and healthy fats in every meal.
Losing weight takes a moderate calorie deficit (≈10–20%). Focus on protein and vegetables — they keep you full at low calories. Don\'t starve yourself — it\'s harmful and ineffective.

Cutting means losing fat while keeping muscle: high protein (≈2–2.5 g per kg), few fast carbs, calorie deficit. Suited for experienced lifters. It\'s a demanding regimen — consult a specialist if you have health issues.

Light meals are soft, simple dishes most people find comfortable. This is NOT a therapeutic diet. If you have pain, discomfort or chronic digestive issues — see a doctor. Self-treating with food can be dangerous.
